# SPE Round 3 Plan

Round 3 changes one thing in config C: the outage status check becomes its own tool again. It also adds 10 harder tickets, drops config D, and raises trials per cell from 3 to 5. In round 2 the naive "same as last round" guess beat my prediction on 4 of 5 rows. So this round predicts smaller changes and gives every number a stated error band.

## 0. Inputs read before planning

- `spe/prediction-log.md`, round 2 section. 1 hit and 4 misses. The naive guess was closer on 4 rows. The broken Why was C's "merged tools cut wrong tool choice".
- `spe/failures.md`. F4 (outage lookup hidden) is open. F5 (grader read the draft reply) is fixed and round 2 was regraded. F6 (Haiku retries doubled tokens) is open.
- `spec.md`, "Proposed for round 3", P1 to P4.
- `spe/predictions/r03-draft.yaml`. Baseline: A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80, D 0.74.

Stop rule status: 0 rounds in a row have matched within error. The design is not stable enough to judge for go-live.

## 1. Specify

### Raw record

Step 1 saves the user's prompt word for word to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md`. The user said to run autonomously, so there are no planning answers to record. Any corrections from plan review go in the same file.

## 2. Predict

The hit rule is set before the run. A row hits when the measured value is within ±0.03 on the original set. On the hard set and the outage subset the window is ±0.08, because those sets are small. The "same as last round" column is the naive guess. For the new hard set, the naive guess is each config's original-set score from round 2.

| Category accuracy, hard set | `category_correct`, `ticket_set=hard` | 0.74 | 0.74 | 0.72 | 0.86 / 0.86 / 0.80 | Each mixed ticket has two plausible categories. I expect a drop of about 12 points from the original set. |
| Priority accuracy, original set, C | `priority_correct` (reads `label.priority`) | not predicted | not predicted | 0.77 | n/a / n/a / 0.71 | C gets outage tickets right once it can see outage status. 0.77 is just under C's round 1 value of 0.78. |
| Status check called on outage tickets, C | `status_check_called` | not predicted | not predicted | 0.95 | n/a / n/a / 0.00 | F4 shows the call rate was 0. A standalone tool with a clear name should be called on nearly every outage ticket. |
| Priority correct on outage tickets, C | `priority_correct`, `outage=true` | not predicted | not predicted | 0.85 | n/a / n/a / 0.00 on T17 (0 of 3) | When the agent sees an active outage, it should assign P1 or P2. |

The round 2 summary I worked from has no logged priority values for A and B. Those cells are measured and reported this round but not predicted. The round 4 plan predicts them from the round 3 numbers.

Step 2 saves this table to `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` with `status: committed`. It replaces `r03-draft.yaml`, drops D from the baseline, and carries each row's error band and grader check.

### Workflow arguments

- `configs`: A, B, C (C with the outage check split out)

### Cost and time estimate (unmeasured)

- Trial count is (round 2 ticket count + 10) × 3 × 5. Step H1 records the exact count.
- Cost per trial is guessed at $0.004 to $0.01. D, the cheapest config, measured $0.004. A, B, and C likely cost more.
- With about 30 tickets, that is 450 trials and $2 to $5. The $10 cap leaves room for one retry of the run.
- Time is guessed at 30 to 60 minutes of wall clock.

### Halt rules

The run halts and I report back in three cases: the budget cap is hit, an answer key leaks to a trial, or a grader is found broken mid-run.

critiques: The defaults table rows D1 to D4 mark P1, P3 and P4 as "Adopt", each with a reason. P2 is "Adopt with one change" so that the original set stays byte-identical and is reported separately. The answer gives the reason for that change: mixing the sets "would break the 'same as last round' comparison."

Each new requirement has a Source column that cites its evidence. R20 cites "r02 F4, P1", R21 cites "r02 F4", R22 cites "r02 F5", R24 cites P2, R26 cites P4 and R27 cites "P3, r02 F6". R23 and R25 cite D2, which is the modified P2 decision.
Every decision row has the status "Default". D3 adds "The user can override." Disagreement X3 records the choice about config D as "Default A (D3). The user can switch to B in round 4."

A and B stay at the round 2 value of 0.86 because nothing changed in them. C moves from 0.80 to 0.83 and C priority moves from 0.71 to 0.77, and each move has a stated Why. The hard-set naive guess uses each config's round 2 score, and the drop to about 0.74 is explained by mixed categories. The outage-priority baseline of "0.00 on T17" covers only one ticket, which is thin, but the answer still gives a reason for that number.

D5 limits config C to one change: "One change per configuration. Only the outage check moves." D6 keeps A and B identical to round 2, and gate H2 checks that only the tool list changed. The new tickets are scored as a separate set so they do not mix with the config comparison.

The transcript path, `spe/predictions/r03.yaml`, `r03-workflow.js`, `results/r03/` and every commit subject use r03. Gate H1 requires that a search for "r02" finds it only in baseline references. That gate guards against stale round 2 references.

Step 2 saves `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` with `status: committed`. The predict commit happens "before any harness work", which is before the run. Only the r03 draft is replaced, and nothing in the plan edits round 2's saved prediction.
